I find it hard to comment in a meaningful way, since it's hard for me to envision exactly how society would change if everyone had legally admissible dirt on everyone.

And maybe it wouldn't change society all that much -- people would have to turn off the cameras when they, say, went to the bathroom, right? And you're presumably not going to leave it on if you're...doing consensual stuff with someone. I envision it would help the most in cases like rape, where the victim would presumably have their camera on, but a simple mask (or darkness?) would render a bodycam useless. If these cameras had GPS on 100% of the time, that might help to figure out who was where, when, but that's a whole 'nother layer of surveillance...and what's to keep someone from just shedding the camera? It would have to be able to read vital signs to prove it was on someone at a given time. But why not have your friend wear two to cover for you? Could anyone prove that you were (or weren't) wearing your camera at any point in time? Could leaving it off at any given time be considered circumstantial evidence of guild?

It just seems dicey to me. What if you forget to turn it on and someone attacks you? Could the lack of video evidence be used against you? Would this become a necessary part of life? Would you have to watch out for areas without a good signal (videos wouldn't upload until signal was reacquired), where attackers might lie in wait?

And let's face it. This kind of a thing means that more criminals would be caught, but that's a double-edged sword. I admittedly did some harmless (but illegal) things as a kid. A friend brought some roman candle things one 4th of July, and we set them off in his backyard. They're not legal in this county. Would the police come after me if video of such an event was leaked? Or could I just turn my camera off whenever I felt like it to avoid such situations -- as long as no one else could see us, we'd be safe? What about minors? Video all the time? None of the time? Parents' discretion?

I'd also worry about improvised electromagnetic devices. Cameras won't help if they're easily disabled by criminals. And, yes, they would find a way to do that. Cheaply and quickly.

I half agree with you. It would definitely change peoples' perspectives. In today's world, the only people ~constantly in the limelight are celebrities. Most of them don't seem to like it, for a variety of reasons. Granted, that's a one-sided "blackmail" relationship since no one cares about what's going on in the paparazzi's lives, but still. Even if ~no one wanted to read the tabloids about you, would you really want it all out there for people to read? Would you care that unknown third parties could be (and would be) watching you in your daily life? Is the ~crime that this kind of change might prevent worth the unknown societal change? How would it affect your chances for getting a job, or for finding a good relationship? It's beyond blackmail. It's big brother. Orwellian. The Handmaid's Tale. 1984.

And you're supporting it. I have no idea what it would be like, but I'm scared as hell that you guys are really toying with an idea like this.

If you really want your money back and CIG won't give it, you may be able to dispute the charge with your bank. Under reason you could say "product not delivered."

I personally am happy waiting, but I also know how it feels to want your money back and be told "sorry, not gonna happen." Lucky for those of us in the USA we have consumer protection laws, so if you want your money back that bad, just look into whether or not you can dispute those charges with your bank. Often times you can do it right on your bank's website.

People are afforded significant rights under consumer protection in the states. Even if they HAD received a product, but it was different from what they expected - that would be enough to dispute. This is taken from my state's laws:

"The types of "billing errors" include:

Charges you did not authorize; Charges for undelivered goods or services; Charges for goods or services different from what was represented or of the wrong quantity; Charges for goods that were not timely delivered
If you want a "refund" your best bet is the gray market. Otherwise I don't think CIG is obligated to give you one.
